content.text: No arbitration or competing forum exists anywhere in the document; the sole clause is Article XXIV / General Provisions (a). Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: The parties agree that any legal suit, action or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement must be instituted in the City of New York, State of New York, and the parties each (i) irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, or any court of the State of New York, and (ii) waives any objection to the venue of any such suit, action or proceeding and any claim relating to forum non conveniens.
input.rationale: The only governing-law/venue provision is General Provisions (a) (p0145-p0146): the Agreement is governed by the internal laws of the State of New York, and all suits must be instituted in the City of New York with irrevocable submission to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Southern District of New York or any New York State court, plus a venue and forum non conveniens waiver. There is no arbitration provision (no responsive text for "arbitration"), no foreign seat, and no competing forum elsewhere in the document. This sits at our preferred position: New York law with exclusive state and federal court jurisdiction in New York. Two immaterial points noted only: the venue is expressed as the "City of New York" rather than New York County (which encompasses Manhattan/New York County and includes the S.D.N.Y. and New York State courts sitting there), and the clause contains no express carve-out for temporary injunctive relief elsewhere — the absence of that carve-out makes exclusivity stronger for us, so no redline is warranted.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
mappings.quote: the validity, interpretation and legal effect of this Agreement shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of New York, U.S.A.

mappings.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
